beats.text: It started at IBA Karachi, with a degree in computer science.
I wanted to know how the things on my screen actually worked.
A learning platform for Kazakhstan's Ministry of Education: the first time strangers used something I made.
React clicked, and interfaces became the thing I couldn't stop thinking about.
Flutter took the same care onto phones.
Since then I've spent 3+ years shipping React and TypeScript for governments, industry and my own products.
I live in the gap between a design file and what people touch: motion, states, edge cases, accessibility.
When something works, I want to know why. When it doesn't, I want to know why faster.

steps.name: Discover
steps.summary: I start by understanding the problem: who it's for, what success looks like, and what could get in the way.

steps.name: Design
steps.summary: I plan the structure and sketch the key screens and interactions before writing code.

steps.name: Build
steps.summary: I build it in small, tested pieces, checking performance and accessibility as I go.

steps.name: Refine
steps.summary: I test on real devices with real people, then polish the details until it feels right.

steps.name: Launch
steps.summary: I ship it, measure how it performs, and keep improving it after launch.
